page.layout: One printed page. Running head at the top, with the page number at the top right. Below it: the emblem title in two lines, then a woodcut illustration across the full width, then a verse passage of four lines with a large initial. Gathering signature at the foot left.

main_text.head: Faber ferrum lima terens, & Rusticus messem flagellans. X VIII.

p.i: QVod duro lima est ferro, messiq; flagellum, Auro quod ignis est rudi: Hoc tibi, si sapias, crux est, licet aspera: quisquis Caelum Deo petis duce.

page.notes: The woodcut shows three labouring men: at left a man swings a flail over a heap of grain; in the centre a man raises a hammer over an anvil-like block; at right a smith in a workshop with a furnace holds a bar of metal on an anvil. The woodcut has no printed text. The word "messiq;" in the verse is set in a ligature that is hard to read, so it is given with [?] in mind; the form is as best read. The first letter of the verse is a large initial Q, joined to "Vod" as "QVod".
